fixes.explanation: Right, baker. The whole congregation threatens to stone Joshua and Caleb, and those two had only said the land was exceedingly good (Numbers 14:7, 10). I think that one stings. Then, right in the middle of all that, the glory of the LORD appears to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting.

That's the word, baker. The LORD asks how long they will refuse to believe in Him, and He points to all the signs He has performed among them (Numbers 14:11). Signs all around, and still the belief won't come. I think that's what makes the question so heavy.

Rejoice is a nice word, but it's not the one the LORD uses. He asks how long they will refuse to believe in Him, despite all the signs He has performed among them (Numbers 14:11). Nobody in this camp is throwing a rejoicing party, friend. That night the people wept (Numbers 14:1). The missing word is believe.

That's it, baker. The LORD says He will do to them just what He heard them say (Numbers 14:28). He had heard their complaints against Him (Numbers 14:27). Earlier they'd said they wished they had died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:2). Now the LORD says their bodies will fall in this wilderness (Numbers 14:29).

Not the other spies, friend. The ones who brought out the bad report were struck down by a plague before the LORD (Numbers 14:37). The LORD says He will bring in the people's children, the ones the people had said would become plunder (Numbers 14:31, 3). The children get the land their parents rejected.

Yes, baker, that's true. Of all the spies, only Joshua and Caleb are still alive (Numbers 14:38). The rest, the men who brought out the bad report, were struck down by a plague before the LORD (Numbers 14:37). Joshua and Caleb were the two who told the congregation the land was exceedingly good (Numbers 14:6, 7).
